transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Lately I keep losing important things for my catering and church work—papers, lists, even ingredients—and it’s starting to mess up events I’m responsible for. It's really starting to worry me and my family, so I wanted to get some help with it.
Have you noticed any difficulties with remembering recent events, learning new information, or following instructions, aside from just losing things?

Yes, I really struggle with following instructions and keeping up with daily tasks. If someone gives me a list of steps to follow, I'll start off fine but then forget the rest of the steps and leave the job half-done. I also keep forgetting everyday things like returning phone calls, paying bills, or showing up to church meetings unless my wife reminds me.
Have you experienced any confusion, disorientation, or difficulty with speaking, reading, or understanding language, in addition to the memory and organizational issues you've described?

No, I don't experience any confusion, disorientation, or trouble with speaking or reading. The only thing close to that is when people are talking to me, my mind sometimes drifts off and I realize I didn't fully catch what they said. It feels more like my attention wanders rather than a problem understanding the words.
Have you noticed these memory and organizational problems gradually worsening over time, or did they seem to start more suddenly?

To be honest, I’ve had tendencies like this since I was a kid, like daydreaming and losing my homework in school. But it has gradually become much more noticeable and problematic over the last 11 months. Once I retired and lost the structure of a regular job, trying to manage my own catering and church projects really made these issues stand out.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by your mind drifting off when people are talking to you, and how often this happens in your daily life?

When my wife or kids are explaining plans or lists to me, I find myself nodding along but realize I didn't actually process what they said. This happens about half the time, so I either have to ask them to repeat themselves or I end up getting the tasks completely wrong.
Do you often find yourself being easily distracted by your surroundings or other stimuli when you're trying to focus on a task, aside from just your mind drifting off during conversations?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed being easily distracted by external noises or things going on around me. It feels more like my own mind just drifts off internally to random thoughts when I'm trying to focus on something.
Do you often find yourself making careless mistakes, such as forgetting to turn off the stove or leaving the door unlocked, due to not paying attention to details?

No, I don't recall making those specific types of careless mistakes like leaving the stove on or doors unlocked. My problems are really more about losing my paperwork and ingredients, or just completely forgetting to finish tasks I've already started.
Do you often have trouble sustaining focus during tasks that require mental effort, such as reading a book or working on a project, and find yourself getting bored or losing interest?

Yes, I definitely struggle with that. When I sit down to plan a catering menu or go over the church festival budget, I can only stay focused for about ten minutes before my mind drifts off. I'll suddenly realize I've just been staring at the paper without actually taking in any of the information.
Have you ever had difficulty waiting for your turn, interrupting others, or blurting out answers before questions are finished being asked, which might suggest impulsivity alongside your inattention?

I haven't really noticed having those kinds of problems with interrupting, blurting things out, or waiting my turn. My struggles have always been much more about my focus, memory, and keeping track of my things.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, or have difficulty engaging in activities quietly, which might suggest symptoms of hyperactivity?

No, I don't really feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying quiet. My issues are much more about losing focus, being disorganized, and forgetting things, rather than being physically hyperactive.

Can you think of any situations where you had to learn new information, like a recipe for your catering or a new procedure at church, and how you managed to remember or forget that information over time?

When I try to learn a new recipe or church procedure, I really struggle to make the information sink in and often just find myself staring at the page. If it involves a list of steps, I might do the first part but then completely forget the rest of the instructions. Plus, I constantly lose the notebooks where I write these things down, making it very hard to refer back to them.
Can you describe a recent situation where you had to recall a specific piece of information, like a phone number or an appointment time, and how you went about trying to remember it?

Just last week, I completely forgot about an important church committee meeting and only made it because my wife reminded me at the last second. Now, to avoid missing catering dates or meetings, I have to write them in giant letters on the kitchen calendar. It’s incredibly frustrating to have to rely on these kinds of workarounds just to keep track of my schedule.

Can you tell me if you think your main problem is with paying attention to details and staying focused, or if it's more about genuinely forgetting things that you once knew, like appointments or how to do tasks?

It definitely feels much more like an issue with paying attention and staying focused rather than forgetting things I once knew. My mind just drifts off so easily when I'm trying to focus, and sometimes I don't even register what people are saying in the first place. This tendency to daydream and lose track of details goes all the way back to my childhood, so it's not like I'm suddenly losing skills or knowledge I used to have.
Have you ever experienced symptoms of hyperactivity, such as feeling excessively restless or having trouble sitting still, especially in quiet environments like church or during meetings?

No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of symptoms. My struggles have always been much more about focus, daydreaming, and keeping track of my things, rather than feeling restless or unable to sit still.
Can you think of a time when you were able to focus and complete a task without getting distracted, and what made that situation different from your usual experiences?

Honestly, I can't really think of a time recently where I was able to just focus easily without my mind eventually drifting off. It has generally felt like a constant struggle to keep my attention on anything for very long.
Can you estimate how often, on average, you are able to complete tasks or projects without needing reminders or assistance from others to stay on track?

It is actually quite difficult for me to finish projects entirely on my own without reminders. While I might start a task just fine, I often lose track of the later steps or forget about them completely until my wife, family, or church colleagues prompt me and ask why it isn't finished yet.

Can you think of any situations where you were able to recall past events or learn new information without significant difficulty, but still struggled with completing tasks or following instructions due to inattention?

I haven't really thought about comparing my memory for past events with my attention like that, so I'm not entirely sure. But I do know my main struggle is definitely with following through on multi-step instructions and actually finishing tasks once I get started on them.

Can you tell me more about whether you think your difficulty with tasks is more because you can't remember the steps or because you have trouble sustaining your attention long enough to complete them?

It is actually a combination of both. When I sit down to do paperwork or planning, my mind drifts off after about ten minutes and I completely lose my focus. At the same time, when I'm given a list of steps to follow, I will start the first part fine but then forget the rest of the instructions until someone asks me about it.
Do you think your main issue is with remembering things, like appointments or tasks, or with staying focused and attentive during activities, like conversations or work projects?

It really feels like a mix of both. For the focus part, my mind drifts off after just ten minutes of planning menus, and I struggle to pay attention during family conversations even when I'm nodding along. On the memory side, I keep forgetting daily tasks like returning phone calls, paying bills, or remembering meetings unless my wife reminds me.

Can you compare how often you forget things you were supposed to do, like appointments or tasks, versus how often you struggle to focus and pay attention during activities, like conversations or planning projects?

Both of these issues happen very frequently and feel closely connected for me. I constantly forget daily tasks like returning calls, paying bills on time, or showing up to meetings without a reminder. At the same time, my focus is just as weak; when I try to plan a budget, my mind drifts off after ten minutes, and in conversations, I often realize I missed half of what was said even though I was nodding.

Do you think your difficulties with tasks and conversations are more due to problems with holding and manipulating information in your working memory, or more with sustaining attention and avoiding mind-wandering?

It really feels like a combination of both. My mind constantly drifts off to random things when I try to focus on planning menus or budgets, which is a big struggle with sustaining attention. But I also have a hard time holding onto information in the moment, which makes me miss what's said in conversations or completely forget the later steps of instructions halfway through a task.

Can you think of any situations where you were able to remember complex information, like a recipe or a church procedure, without difficulty, but still struggled to complete the task due to lack of focus or attention?

Yes, I actually know my recipes and church procedures very well from years of experience, so remembering how to do them isn't the problem. The struggle is really in the execution—when I sit down to plan a menu, my mind drifts off after ten minutes, or when doing a multi-step task I know well, I'll start off fine but lose focus after the first step and fail to follow through.
Can you describe a situation where you were able to focus and remember all the steps of a task without difficulty, and how that differed from your usual experience with tasks and conversations?

To be honest, I can't recall a recent situation where I was able to focus and remember all the steps of a task without any difficulty. Ever since I retired and lost the external structure of my old job, everything has felt very scattered. I really can't think of a single time lately where I didn't struggle with distraction or forgetfulness.
Can you think of any times when you were able to remember and recall complex information, like a recipe or a procedure, but still had trouble completing the task due to lack of focus or attention?

Yes, that actually happens quite often. Even when I know a recipe or a church setup procedure perfectly, I will start the first part just fine but then get distracted or lose focus halfway through. My mind will just drift off, leaving the rest of the task completely unfinished until someone points it out to me.

Can you think of any tasks where you were able to focus and complete them without difficulty, but still had trouble recalling specific details or instructions later on, which might help distinguish between problems with attention versus problems with memory?

I’m not quite sure, and I haven't really noticed a situation like that happening. For me, it usually feels like my mind drifts off or I lose track of things right from the very start, rather than being able to focus well on a task and then forgetting the details later.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, or ADHD, in the past, especially considering your long-standing issues with focus and organization?

No, I have never been formally diagnosed or treated for ADHD before, and this is my first time seeking a psychiatric evaluation. Although my teachers back in elementary school always noted that I was daydreaming and disorganized, it was never recognized or treated as ADHD when I was growing up. We just didn't really think about those things back then.

Can you think of any tasks where you were able to recall all the steps and details without difficulty, but still had trouble completing them due to lack of focus or getting distracted, which might help us understand if your main issue is with sustaining attention or with working memory?

It's really hard for me to separate the two because they seem to happen right together. Often, I don't just get distracted while remembering the steps; I actually completely forget what the next steps are in the middle of a task. Because of that, I'm not entirely sure which one is the main culprit since they always seem to overlap.

Can you think of any situations where you were able to recall complex information without difficulty, but still struggled to complete tasks due to lack of focus, which might help us understand whether your main issue is with attention or working memory?

I'm not quite sure, as I've never really thought about trying to separate my memory from my focus like that. I just know that when I sit down to plan something, my mind drifts off easily, or I'll lose track of the steps halfway through a task. It's hard for me to tell if that is because of an attention issue or a memory problem.

Can you describe a situation where you were able to focus and complete a task without difficulty, but later had trouble recalling the details of what you did, which might help us distinguish between problems with attention and problems with memory?

I can't really recall a specific situation like that. Usually, my issues seem to happen right in the moment—like my mind drifting off or losing track of things while I'm actually doing them—rather than me focusing perfectly and then forgetting it all later.

Can you tell me if there's ever a time when you're able to recall a task or instructions perfectly, but still struggle to initiate or complete it due to lack of motivation or interest, rather than forgetfulness or distraction?

I haven't really noticed motivation or interest being the issue, because I actually care a lot about my catering and church work and really want to do them. My main struggle is just that I genuinely get distracted, forget what I'm doing, or lose the paperwork and items I need to get the job done.
